# Governance With TERM Token Veto Configuration Proof

## 1. High Level Conclusion

```
Branch 1 (the slow path, for real proposals)
  ProposerSafe (5/11) ------module------> Delay Modifier ------module------> OwnerlessSafe (9/9) ------DEVOPS_ROLE------> Term Protocol
  (+ ConfigLockGuard)                     (+ PauseGuard)                  (+ ConfigLockGuard)

Direct path (all nine OwnerlessSafe signers together: no delay, veto or pause)
  OwnerlessSafe (9/9) ------DEVOPS_ROLE------> Term Protocol

Branch 2 (the token-vote path, whose only power is to veto)
  Governor ------module------> Roles Modifier ------target------> DelayOwnerSafe ------owner------> Delay Modifier
                            (+ SetTxNonceGuard)                 (+ ConfigLockGuard)

Pause controls
  PauseSafe (2/9) --pause-->               PauseGuard
  ProposerSafe   --unpause / setPauser-->  PauseGuard
```

**Trust assumption:** Despite its name, the OwnerlessSafe has nine Term multisig holders as owners and a threshold of 9, high enough that its direct path has more friction than going through the Delay Modifier.

The conclusions drawn from these proofs establish the following propositions:

1. The Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe and the Term multisig holders on the OwnerlessSafe, and only they, may execute DEVOPS_ROLE methods, holding: 1. the owners, fallbackHandler, modules, and guard constant for the ProposerSafe and OwnerlessSafe, and the module guard constant for the OwnerlessSafe; 2. the owner, target, modules, guard, txCooldown, and txExpiration constant for the Delay Modifier; and 3. the pauser and admin constant for the PauseGuard, provided DEVOPS_ROLE method calls from the ProposerSafe are not vetoed, and are executed while the PauseGuard is not paused and before the 24-hour expiration period following the cooldown ends.

2. Only TERM token holders, through a proposal made by a holder with at least 1,000 TERM of voting power that reaches a quorum of 1,000,000 TERM, if proposed within 2 hours of the transaction being queued, and Term multisig holders may veto Delay Modifier transactions within the 24-hour veto window, in which a Delay Modifier transaction cannot be executed until txCooldown has passed since it was queued, holding: 1. the owners, fallbackHandler, modules, guard, module guard constant for the DelayOwnerSafe, and 2. the owner, target, modules, guard constant for the Delay Modifier and Roles Modifier, and 3. the role targets, role scopes, role assignments constant for the Roles Modifier, and 4. the voting token, proposal threshold, voting threshold, quorum constant for the Governor, and 5. the txCooldown constant for the Delay Modifier.

3. Only the Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe may pause, and only the Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe may unpause, the execution of Delay Modifier transactions, and if a pause outlasts the 24-hour expiration period following the cooldown, the Delay Modifier transaction can only be skipped or vetoed, holding: 1. the owners, fallbackHandler, modules, guard constant for the PauseSafe and ProposerSafe, and 2. the guard, txCooldown, txExpiration constant for the Delay Modifier, and 3. the pauser and admin constant for the PauseGuard.

4. The following: 1. the owner, target, modules, guard, role targets, role scopes, role assignments for the Roles Modifier, and 2. the voting token, proposal threshold, voting threshold, quorum for the Governor cannot be changed by anyone.

5. The owners for the ProposerSafe, OwnerlessSafe, and DelayOwnerSafe can be changed only by the Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe, OwnerlessSafe, or DelayOwnerSafe. The fallbackHandler, modules, guard, module guard for the OwnerlessSafe can be changed only by the Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe. The following: 1. the fallbackHandler, modules, guard for the ProposerSafe and DelayOwnerSafe, 2. the module guard for the DelayOwnerSafe, and 3. the owner, target, modules, guard, txCooldown, txExpiration for the Delay Modifier cannot be changed by anyone.

6. The owners, fallbackHandler, modules, guard for the PauseSafe can be changed only by the Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe. The pauser for the PauseGuard can be changed only by the Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe. The admin for the PauseGuard cannot be changed by anyone.

Only Term multisig holders can execute DEVOPS_ROLE methods subject to TERM token governance, and this cannot be changed other than through Term multisig approval.

## 2. Evidence Classification

This document uses two classes of evidence to establish the security and functional properties of the governance configuration:

- **Formal Verification (FV) evidence** establishes that, assuming the stated configuration, the relevant contracts enforce the claimed security and functional properties. These properties are proved with the Certora Prover, a formal verification tool. For the guards (PauseGuard, ConfigLockGuard and SetTxNonceGuard), the proofs run on the contract code that was deployed, the code at commit [`e9f3d20f4d16af7ab7a9fdf773e4fabd4cde3353`](https://github.com/term-finance/zodiac-modifier-roles-v1/commit/e9f3d20f4d16af7ab7a9fdf773e4fabd4cde3353) on `main`. For TERM, the Governor rules that read TERM run on the code the TERM proxy is to be upgraded to, the code at commit [`74b19ca41aebf28c5b7801e94f082aad867b0f17`](https://github.com/term-finance/term-token/commit/74b19ca41aebf28c5b7801e94f082aad867b0f17) on term-token `main`. For the Governor, the proofs run on term-finance-ops-contracts' `TermFinanceProtocolGovernor.sol` at commit [`5d90281be203389bdc465963164f635048e5f3e6`](https://github.com/term-finance/term-finance-ops-contracts/commit/5d90281be203389bdc465963164f635048e5f3e6), the head of PR 1096, built with OpenZeppelin 5.6.1. The proofs cover privileged entry points, authorized callers, configuration immutability, the absence of alternative execution paths, and the intended functionality. In the tables below, FV evidence is labeled **FV —** and names each Certora rule; ✅ marks a rule that passes.
- **Deployment evidence** states the configuration the 2.1.0 deployment must have for the formal verification evidence to apply: owners, modules, guards, thresholds, roles, and other relevant state. 2.1.0 is a proposal, not a live deployment, so none of it has been read on chain yet. In the tables below, deployment evidence is labeled **On-chain —**; ⏳ marks a requirement to verify against on-chain state, at a stated block, once the 2.1.0 contracts are deployed.

These two classes of evidence are complementary. Formal verification evidence does not by itself establish that the deployed contracts have the configuration being proved, and deployment evidence does not by itself establish that the deployed configuration enforces the claimed security and functional properties.

**Safe versions.** This document assumes every Safe in this configuration, the ProposerSafe, OwnerlessSafe, DelayOwnerSafe and PauseSafe, runs Safe v1.5.0, the non-L2 build. The formal verification evidence covers Safe v1.5.0 only.

Configuration items marked ⏳ (pending deployment) describe the configuration of the proposed 2.1.0 deployment and are not established yet. Each must be verified against on-chain state once the 2.1.0 contracts are deployed.

That stays true at every later time, so a transaction whose window ended during the pause cannot be executed after the unpause either.<br>• DM-12 `anyoneCanSkipExpired` ✅ passes: whether a call to `executeNextTx` or `skipExpired` succeeds, and what it changes, does not depend on who the caller is. So a transaction whose window ended during the pause can be skipped during the pause.<br>• The Owner of Delay Modifier can also move `txNonce` past it with a veto, `setTxNonce` (P2.2).<br>• DP-30 `entryPassedByTxNonceNeverExecutes` ✅ passes: once `txNonce` is past the entry, `executeNextTx` with that entry's transaction reverts, unless the same transaction has been queued again and sits at `txNonce`. Queuing it again makes a new entry, with its own veto window.<br><br>**On-chain — The PauseGuard is the Delay Modifier's guard, and it is not paused:**<br>• ⏳ pending deployment. `guard()` on the Delay Modifier must return the PauseGuard, as in P1.13.<br>• ⏳ pending deployment. `paused()` on the PauseGuard must return false.<br><br>**On-chain — The Delay Modifier's expiration period is 24 hours:**<br>• ⏳ pending deployment. `txExpiration()` on the Delay Modifier must be 86,400 seconds (24 hours), as in P1.13. |

The only Module of DelayOwnerSafe is the Roles Modifier (P5.DelayOwnerSafe.4), and by P5.DelayOwnerSafe.5 to P5.DelayOwnerSafe.9 nobody can change them through it, so nobody can change them.<br><br>**On-chain — DelayOwnerSafe guard is ConfigLockGuard:**<br>• ⏳ pending deployment. So the Governor cannot change the Delay Modifier's owner, target, modules, guard, txCooldown or txExpiration.<br><br>**On-chain — The SetTxNonceGuard is the Roles Modifier's guard and is pointed at the Delay Modifier:**<br>• ⏳ pending deployment. `guard()` on the Roles Modifier must return the SetTxNonceGuard, and `getGuard()` must return the same address.<br>• ⏳ pending deployment. `delay()` on the SetTxNonceGuard must return the Delay Modifier, and `target()` on the Roles Modifier must return the DelayOwnerSafe, not the Roles Modifier itself.<br><br>**On-chain — Governor is assigned only Role 1:**<br>• Same as P5.DelayModifier.11.<br><br>**Already proven — SetTxNonceGuard cannot be changed by anyone:**<br>• See P4.RolesModifier: the Roles Modifier's guard, the SetTxNonceGuard, cannot be changed by anyone. by anyone.                                                                                                                                                                 | **FV — The Term multisig holders on the DelayOwnerSafe cannot change the owner, target, modules, guard, txCooldown or txExpiration of the Delay Modifier through `execTransaction` if DelayOwnerSafe guard is ConfigLockGuard, so nobody can change them:**<br>• CL150-6 `checkTransactionRejectsModifierOwnershipChange`, CL150-7 `checkTransactionRejectsModifierModuleChange`, CL150-8 `checkTransactionRejectsModifierSetGuard`, CL150-9 `checkTransactionRejectsModifierSetAvatarOrTarget` ✅ pass: called by the Safe, the guard reverts on any transaction to its locked modifier carrying `transferOwnership`, `renounceOwnership`, `enableModule`, `disableModule`, `setGuard`, `setAvatar` or `setTarget`.<br>• CL150-24 `checkTransactionRejectsModifierTimingChange` ✅ passes: called by the Safe, the guard reverts on any transaction to its locked modifier carrying `setTxCooldown` or `setTxExpiration`.<br>• CL150-23 `guardedSafeCannotCallLockedModifierFunctions` ✅ passes: with ConfigLockGuard installed, an `execTransaction` addressed to the locked modifier with any of these calls reverts, whatever the arguments, value and operation.<br>• CL150-1 `checkTransactionRejectsDelegateCall`, CL150-16 `guardedSafeCannotDelegateCall` ✅ pass: the guard rejects every delegate call, so every `execTransaction` to the Delay Modifier that succeeds is a plain call carrying some other selector.<br>• OD150-1 `unlockedDelayCallsNeverChangeOwnerGuardAvatarOrTarget`, OD150-2 `unlockedDelayCallsNeverChangeModules` ✅ pass: over every Delay Modifier write function except those nine and `setUp`, and for any caller, the owner, guard, target and module list do not change.<br>• OD150-5 `unlockedDelayCallsNeverChangeTxCooldownOrTxExpiration` ✅ passes: over the same functions and any caller, txCooldown and txExpiration do not change.<br>• An `execTransaction` to any other address reaches the Delay Modifier, if at all, with that address as the caller, not the owner, so it cannot change these settings (P5.DelayModifier.2).<br>• The CL150 rules leave `lockedDelay` unconstrained, so they lock whichever modifier ConfigLockGuard was built with. The deployed guard's locked modifier is the Delay Modifier (below).<br>• By P5.DelayModifier.2 and P5.DelayModifier.3, only the DelayOwnerSafe can change the owner, target, modules, guard, txCooldown and txExpiration. The DelayOwnerSafe acts only through `execTransaction` or its modules (P5.DelayModifier.4, P5.DelayModifier.5). Its only module is the Roles Modifier (P5.DelayModifier.7), through which nobody can change them (P5.DelayModifier.8 to P5.DelayModifier.12), so nobody can change them.<br><br>**On-chain — DelayOwnerSafe guard is ConfigLockGuard, with the Delay Modifier as its locked modifier:**<br>• Same as P5.DelayOwnerSafe.10: the DelayOwnerSafe's guard slot must hold ConfigLockGuard.<br>• ⏳ pending deployment. `lockedDelay()` on ConfigLockGuard must return the Delay Modifier.<br>• Assumes the DelayOwnerSafe runs Safe v1.5.0, the version CL150 and OD150 check. |

By P1.2, `execTransaction` only acts once all nine Owners of OwnerlessSafe, the Term multisig holders (P1.4), have approved (SE150-5, SE150-12), and their approvals pass it (SE150-6).<br><br>**FV — The Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe can change the owners, fallbackHandler, modules, guard and module guard of the OwnerlessSafe through the Delay Modifier:**<br>• PO150-5 `proposerApprovalChangesOwnerlessSettings` ✅ passes, for each of `enableModule`, `disableModule`, `addOwnerWithThreshold`, `removeOwner`, `swapOwner`, `changeThreshold`, `setGuard`, `setFallbackHandler` and `setModuleGuard`, in one execution:<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;◦ An owner of the ProposerSafe (a Term multisig holder, P1.11) approves with `approveHash` the hash of the ProposerSafe's call to the Delay Modifier's `execTransactionFromModule(OwnerlessSafe, 0, <settings call>, Call)`, and anyone submits it through `execTransaction` with that approval as the signature.<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;◦ The ProposerSafe is the Delay Modifier's module (P1.8), so the Delay Modifier queues the proposal.<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;◦ Once the cooldown has passed and before the proposal expires, anyone's `executeNextTx` hands it to the Delay Modifier's target, the OwnerlessSafe, which has the Delay Modifier as its module (P1.5).<br>&nbsp;&nbsp;◦ The OwnerlessSafe's `execTransactionFromModule` makes it call its own settings function, and the setting changes.<br>• PO150-5 sets the ProposerSafe's threshold to 1. By SE150-6 (P1.9), with the real threshold of 5 (P1.11), five owners' approvals take the same path.<br>• PO150-5 assumes no guard on either Safe or on the Delay Modifier. The Delay Modifier's guard is the PauseGuard. DP-18 `checkTransactionAcceptsWhileNotPaused` ✅ passes: while not paused, the PauseGuard accepts any transaction. Its `checkAfterExecution` does nothing (`PauseGuard.sol:123`), so with the PauseGuard not paused, PO150-5's path is unchanged.<br>• The ProposerSafe's guard is ConfigLockGuard (P5.ProposerSafe.5). The ProposerSafe's call is to the Delay Modifier's `execTransactionFromModule`, which is not one of the guard's locked calls. CL150-10 `checkTransactionAcceptsEverythingElse` ✅ passes: whatever `lockedDelay` is, the guard accepts every plain call that is not a locked call. It checks ConfigLockGuard's `checkTransaction` directly, so the Safe version does not matter. Its `checkAfterExecution` does nothing (`ConfigLockGuard.sol:141`), so PO150-5's ProposerSafe step is unchanged.<br>• The OwnerlessSafe's guard is ConfigLockGuard (below), but it is never consulted on this path: Safe v1.5.0 consults its guard only in `execTransaction` (`Safe.sol:149-204`), not in `execTransactionFromModule` (`ModuleManager.sol:154-163`, which consults only the module guard, `ModuleManager.sol:94-109`). LG150-2 `moduleCanStillChangeEachSetting` ✅ passes: with ConfigLockGuard installed and its `lockedDelay` the Delay Modifier (P5.DelayModifier.13), an `execTransactionFromModule` from the Delay Modifier, as an enabled module, addressed to the Safe with a call to each of `enableModule`, `disableModule`, `addOwnerWithThreshold`, `removeOwner`, `swapOwner`, `changeThreshold`, `setGuard`, `setFallbackHandler` and `setModuleGuard` succeeds and a setting changes.<br>• PO150-5 assumes the deployed wiring: the ProposerSafe is a module of the Delay Modifier (P1.8), and the Delay Modifier is a module of the OwnerlessSafe (P1.5). The Delay Modifier's target is the OwnerlessSafe and its guard is the PauseGuard, read in P1.13. The OwnerlessSafe's module guard, which would check this path's module transaction, must be `address(0)`, also read in P1.13; PO150-5 and LG150-2 run with it unset.<br>• While the PauseGuard is paused, it rejects every `executeNextTx` (`PauseGuard.sol:119`), so the proposal waits until the PauseGuard's admin unpauses it. If `txExpiration` passes first, the proposal expires and has to be proposed again.<br><br>**FV — The Term multisig holders on the OwnerlessSafe cannot change OwnerlessSafe fallbackHandler, Modules of OwnerlessSafe, OwnerlessSafe guard or OwnerlessSafe module guard through `execTransaction` if OwnerlessSafe guard is ConfigLockGuard, so only the Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe can change them:**<br>• CL150-2 `checkTransactionRejectsSelfSetGuard`, CL150-3 `checkTransactionRejectsSelfEnableModule`, CL150-4 `checkTransactionRejectsSelfDisableModule`, CL150-5 `checkTransactionRejectsSelfSetFallbackHandler` ✅ pass: called by the Safe, the guard reverts on any transaction to the Safe itself carrying `setGuard`, `enableModule`, `disableModule` or `setFallbackHandler`.<br>• CL150-12 `guardedSafeCannotCallSetGuard`, CL150-13 `guardedSafeCannotCallEnableModule`, CL150-14 `guardedSafeCannotCallDisableModule`, CL150-15 `guardedSafeCannotCallSetFallbackHandler` ✅ pass: with ConfigLockGuard installed, an `execTransaction` addressed to the Safe with any of these calls reverts.<br>• CL150-17 `guardedSelfCallNeverChangesGuard`, CL150-18 `guardedSelfCallNeverChangesModules`, CL150-19 `guardedSelfCallNeverChangesFallbackHandler` ✅ pass: for any calldata and operation, an `execTransaction` addressed to the Safe leaves the guard, every entry of the Modules of OwnerlessSafe list and the fallbackHandler unchanged.<br>• CL150-25 `checkTransactionRejectsSelfSetModuleGuard`, CL150-26 `guardedSafeCannotCallSetModuleGuard`, CL150-27 `guardedSelfCallNeverChangesModuleGuard` ✅ pass: called by the Safe, the guard reverts on any transaction to the Safe itself carrying `setModuleGuard`; with ConfigLockGuard installed, an `execTransaction` addressed to the Safe with that call reverts; and for any calldata and operation, an `execTransaction` addressed to the Safe leaves the module guard unchanged.<br>• CL150-1 `checkTransactionRejectsDelegateCall`, CL150-16 `guardedSafeCannotDelegateCall` ✅ pass: the guard rejects every delegate call, so no delegated code can write the guard, the Modules of OwnerlessSafe list, the fallbackHandler or the module guard directly.<br>• By P1.2, these settings only change when the caller is the Safe itself (SE150-7), so an `execTransaction` to any other address cannot change them either.<br>• These rules run on Safe v1.5.0, the OwnerlessSafe's code (P1.2), and leave `lockedDelay` unconstrained, so they hold whichever modifier ConfigLockGuard was built with.<br>• By P5.OwnerlessSafe.2 and P5.OwnerlessSafe.4, only Owners of OwnerlessSafe or Modules of OwnerlessSafe can change the fallbackHandler and the Modules of OwnerlessSafe list, and SC150-4 (P5.OwnerlessSafe.2) covers the guard and the module guard the same way. The only Module of OwnerlessSafe is the Delay Modifier (P5.OwnerlessSafe.4), which only runs transactions queued by Modules of Delay Modifier (P5.OwnerlessSafe.5, P5.OwnerlessSafe.6). The only Module of Delay Modifier is the ProposerSafe, which cannot be changed by anyone (P5.OwnerlessSafe.7), and only the Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe can make the ProposerSafe act (P5.OwnerlessSafe.8 to P5.OwnerlessSafe.11). So only the Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe can change them.<br><br>**On-chain — OwnerlessSafe guard is ConfigLockGuard:**<br>• ⏳ pending deployment. The guard slot (`0x4a204f620c8c5ccdca3fd54d003badd85ba500436a431f0cbda4f558c93c34c8`, `GuardManager.sol:66` in Safe v1.5.0) on the OwnerlessSafe must hold ConfigLockGuard.<br>• Assumes the OwnerlessSafe runs Safe v1.5.0, the version CL150, LG150 and PO150-5 check (`GuardManager.sol:66`). |

### Proposition 6 — The owners, fallbackHandler, modules, guard for the PauseSafe can be changed only by the Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe. The pauser for the PauseGuard can be changed only by the Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe. The admin for the PauseGuard cannot be changed by anyone.

---

#### PauseSafe

##### P6.PauseSafe: The owners, fallbackHandler, modules, guard for the PauseSafe can only be changed by Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe.

| # | Statement | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |

| P6.PauseSafe.2 | PauseSafe fallbackHandler is `address(0)`, which can only be changed by Owners of PauseSafe and Modules of PauseSafe. | Same as P3.Pause.4.<br><br>**FV — PauseSafe fallbackHandler can only be changed by Owners of PauseSafe or Modules of PauseSafe:**<br>• SC150-4 `settingsOnlyChangeThroughAModuleOrOwners` ✅ passes: over every write function, `fallback` included while no fallbackHandler is set (P3.Pause.4), the fallbackHandler only changes through an enabled module's `execTransactionFromModule` or `execTransactionFromModuleReturnData`, or through `execTransaction`.<br>• By P6.PauseSafe.1, only Modules of PauseSafe can call `execTransactionFromModule` and `execTransactionFromModuleReturnData` (SE150-3), and `execTransaction` only acts once as many Owners of PauseSafe as the threshold have approved (SE150-5, SE150-12). So only Modules of PauseSafe or Owners of PauseSafe can change the fallbackHandler. |
| P6.PauseSafe.3 | `Modules of PauseSafe = null`, which can only be changed by Owners of PauseSafe because `Modules of PauseSafe = null`. | Same as P3.Pause.6.<br><br>**FV — Modules of PauseSafe can only be changed by Owners of PauseSafe because `Modules of PauseSafe = null`:**<br>• SC150-4 `settingsOnlyChangeThroughAModuleOrOwners` ✅ passes: over every write function, `fallback` included while no fallbackHandler is set (P3.Pause.4), the module list only changes through an enabled module's `execTransactionFromModule` or `execTransactionFromModuleReturnData`, or through `execTransaction`.<br>• By P6.PauseSafe.1, only Modules of PauseSafe can call `execTransactionFromModule` and `execTransactionFromModuleReturnData` (SE150-3), and `execTransaction` only acts once as many Owners of PauseSafe as the threshold have approved (SE150-5, SE150-12).<br>• The PauseSafe has no module (P3.Pause.6), so only the Owners of PauseSafe can change the module list. |
| P6.PauseSafe.4 | `Owners of PauseSafe = Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe`, which can only be changed by Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe because `Modules of PauseSafe = null`. | Same as P3.Pause.5.<br><br>**FV — Owners of PauseSafe can only be changed by Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe because `Modules of PauseSafe = null`:**<br>• SC150-4 `settingsOnlyChangeThroughAModuleOrOwners` ✅ passes: over every write function, `fallback` included while no fallbackHandler is set (P3.Pause.4), the owners and threshold only change through an enabled module's `execTransactionFromModule` or `execTransactionFromModuleReturnData`, or through `execTransaction`.<br>• By P6.PauseSafe.1, only Modules of PauseSafe can call `execTransactionFromModule` and `execTransactionFromModuleReturnData` (SE150-3), and `execTransaction` only acts once two Owners of PauseSafe, the Term multisig holders (P3.Pause.5), have approved (SE150-5, SE150-12).<br>• The PauseSafe has no module (P3.Pause.6), so only the Term multisig holders on the PauseSafe can change the owners and threshold. |

#### PauseGuard

##### P6.PauseGuard: The pauser for the PauseGuard can only be changed by Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe; the admin for the PauseGuard cannot be changed by anyone.

| # | Statement | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P6.PauseGuard.1 | Only the PauseGuard pauser and the PauseGuard admin can interact with the PauseGuard, except `checkTransaction` and `checkAfterExecution`, which anyone can call but which do not change state.                                                                                                     | Same as P3.1. |
| P6.PauseGuard.2 | `PauseGuard admin = ProposerSafe`, which cannot be changed by anyone.             | Same as P3.Admin.2.<br><br>**FV — Nobody can change the PauseGuard admin:**<br>• DP-14 `adminNeverChanges` ✅ passes: over every write function of the Delay Modifier and the PauseGuard, the admin never changes.<br>• `admin` is `immutable` (`PauseGuard.sol:17`), set once in the constructor, so no function can write it. |
| P6.PauseGuard.3 | `PauseGuard pauser = PauseSafe`, which can only be changed by Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe. | Same as P3.Pause.2.<br><br>**FV — The PauseGuard pauser can only be changed by Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe:**<br>• DP-13 `pauserOnlyChangesThroughSetPauser` ✅ passes: over every write function of both contracts, the pauser only changes through `setPauser`.<br>• DP-10 `setPauserRevertsForAnyoneButTheAdmin` ✅ passes: anyone who is not the admin is rejected.<br>• The PauseGuard admin is the ProposerSafe (P6.PauseGuard.2), and only the Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe can make it act (P5.ProposerSafe.1, P5.ProposerSafe.3, P5.ProposerSafe.4). So only they can change the pauser. |
| P6.PauseGuard.4 | The pauser for the PauseGuard can be changed by Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe; the admin for the PauseGuard cannot be changed by Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe, so it cannot be changed by anyone.             | **FV — The Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe can change the PauseGuard pauser:**<br>• DP-11 `setPauserSetsThePauser` ✅ passes: for any nonzero account, the admin's `setPauser(account)` succeeds, `pauser()` then returns that account, and the previous pauser no longer holds the slot.<br>• SE150-6 `ownersCanMakeTheSafeAct` ✅ passes: once the threshold is passed, `execTransaction` succeeds and the Safe acts, for any threshold and any number of owners. So the ProposerSafe's owners (P3.Admin.5) can have it call `setPauser`.<br>• The ProposerSafe's guard is ConfigLockGuard (P5.ProposerSafe.5). Its call to `setPauser` on the PauseGuard is a plain call to neither the ProposerSafe nor its locked Delay Modifier, so it is not a locked call. CL150-10 `checkTransactionAcceptsEverythingElse` ✅ passes: whatever `lockedDelay` is, the guard accepts every plain call that is not a locked call. It checks ConfigLockGuard's `checkTransaction` directly, so the Safe version does not matter. Its `checkAfterExecution` does nothing (`ConfigLockGuard.sol:141`), so the call is unchanged.<br><br>**FV — The Term multisig holders on the ProposerSafe cannot change the PauseGuard admin, so nobody can:**<br>• Same as P6.PauseGuard.2: the admin never changes, whoever the caller is, the ProposerSafe included. |
